transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um… I guess I’m here because I’ve been having a hard time at work. It’s probably not as bad as it sounds, but I can’t really make myself go near the front windows anymore, or even that part of the street outside. I keep finding reasons to stay in the back, even though being up front is part of my job. I know that probably isn’t great, so… I thought I should talk to someone.
When you avoid the front windows and that part of the street, is it because you’re worried about something specific happening, like a panic attack, being judged by others, or something else?

I don’t think it’s really about being judged or anything like that. And I wouldn’t want to call it a panic attack exactly… I just, um, when I’m near the front windows or that part of the street, I feel like I need to get away from it. So I’ve been making excuses to stay in the back, even though I know that’s part of my job. Does that make sense?
Has something happened to you in the past that connects to the front windows or that part of the street, like a frightening or upsetting experience?

Yeah… there was. I probably should’ve said that sooner, sorry. About two weeks ago, during an overnight shift, a car crashed through the store window. Since then, that whole front area and the street right there have just been… harder to be around.
Since the accident, have you found yourself re-living it in your mind, like having flashbacks or upsetting memories when you’re near the front windows?

Yeah… I mean, not all the time, I don’t want to make it sound dramatic. But it does kind of pop into my head when I’m not expecting it. Like if I’m trying to set up displays near the front, suddenly I can hear that bang again, and I can see the glass coming down, almost like it’s happening right then. Is that the kind of thing you mean?

latest_inference.note: The patient described re-living the traumatic event through intrusive memories and flashbacks, which aligns with the diagnostic criteria for post-traumatic stress disorder (F43.10). There is no indication of agoraphobia (F40.00) as the avoidance is specifically tied to a traumatic event rather than a generalized fear of places or panic attacks.
